title: Gemini Harness Decoupling & Delegation Lessons
desc: Lessons learned from wkappbot-kih extraction: PowerShell interpolation bugs, bash shadowing, proactive API usage, and granular model tiering.
steps: 1. PROACTIVE API USAGE: Do not halt when an existing tool script (e.g., gmail_manager.py) lacks support for a specific account. Check the global .env file for existing OAuth tokens and write a direct API script (e.g., gmail_send.py) to fulfill the user's intent.

2. POWERSHELL INTERPOLATION TRAP: When using string replacement (Python/sed) to patch .ps1 files, do not accidentally convert double quotes to single quotes. Single quotes block variable interpolation (e.g., '\'), causing CommandNotFoundException during subagent delegation.

3. BASH SHADOWING: In the WKAppBot ecosystem, calling 'bash' from PowerShell might resolve to 'WKAppBot/bin/Bash.cmd'. When invoking .sh wrappers (like wkgemini.sh), explicitly use Git Bash (C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe) to avoid syntax errors.

4. STALL-GUARD MODEL PARSING: Avoid monolithic tier mapping for diverse model families. Parse \ to map Gemini Flash to Haiku-tier (3m) and Gemini Pro to Sonnet-tier (6m). Reserve Opus for top-tier orchestrator blocks.
5. MARKDOWN ENCODING: Always save .md files as UTF-8 without BOM (use Python encoding='utf-8' without -sig).
